## Overview

QTSim follows one trait. QTLSim can follow `n` of them at once (`NoTraits = n`): every
locus carries a vector of `n` allelic effects, so a mutation can change several traits
together (pleiotropy), and selection acts on the traits jointly through a fitness
function in `n` dimensions. This is the classical multivariate quantitative genetics of
@Lande1979 and @Lande1980, in which the additive genetic covariance matrix `G` takes
the place of the genetic variance, and of the simulation studies of `G`'s stability by
@Jones2003, @Jones2004 and @Jones2007.

The life cycle does not change. The model of several traits is a second family of
lowerings of the same morphism of the life-cycle category: each step is sent to an
operator on populations whose genotypes are vectors rather than numbers, and the steps
that do not care what an allele is (inheritance, the change of width, the swap of
generations) are sent to the same operators as for one trait. The design note
[Several traits](https://ecorecipes.github.io/QTLSim.jl/dev/traits_design/) records
what generalised and what did not. This vignette shows the model, checks the `G` matrix
it maintains against theory, and follows the correlated response to a moving optimum,
the effect of the mutational correlation, local adaptation of several demes in two
traits, and an optimum that fluctuates.

## Setup

```{julia}
using QTLSim
using QTLSim: eigen, Symmetric, norm, dot   # LinearAlgebra, through the package
import Catlab                                # loads the categorical layer
using Catlab: ⋅, ⊗
using CairoMakie, Printf, Random, Statistics
CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png")
L = lifecycle(); g = L.generation            # QTSim's generation, Zygotes → Zygotes
```

## The model

With `NoTraits = 2`, three things become matrices. The phenotype is `z = g + e`, with
the genotype `g` the sum of the loci's effect vectors and `e ~ N(0, V_E I)`. A mutation
adds a draw from `N(0, M/(2L·rate))` to the effect vector of a random locus, so that the
expected input per individual per generation is the mutational covariance `M`: here
`m V_E` on the diagonal scaled by a shape `[1 0.5; 0.5 0.6]`, given as `MutCov`. Fitness is
QTSim's Gaussian in two dimensions, `W(z) = c·exp(−½ (z−θ)ᵀ Ω⁻¹ (z−θ))`, with QTSim's
constant `c` and `Ω = ω² S`, here with a correlation of −0.3 between the two traits'
fitness (`SelCorr`). The two matrices do not share eigenvectors.

```{julia}
p = Params(PopSize = 1000, NoQTL = 20, Ploidy = 2, NoGenerations = 3000, PhenotypeVar = 1.0,
           Heritability = 0.5, MutationScalar = 0.01, MutationRatePerGamete = 0.02,
           RecombPoissonMean = 2.0, InitFitnessSD = 1.5, NoTraits = 2,
           MutCov = 0.01 * 0.5 .* [1.0 0.5; 0.5 0.6], SelCorr = -0.3)
M, Ω = mutational_covariance(p), selection_covariance(p)
@printf("M = [%.4f %.4f; %.4f %.4f], Ω = [%.3f %.3f; %.3f %.3f], V_E = %.2f per trait\n",
        M[1, 1], M[1, 2], M[2, 1], M[2, 2], Ω[1, 1], Ω[1, 2], Ω[2, 1], Ω[2, 2], envVar(p))
```

The parameters a step can carry belong to the model. `model_of(p)` is the model of
`TraitModel(2)`, and its schema says what each step takes; for one trait `select`'s
optimum `θ` is a number, for two it is a vector, and only the model of several traits has
a fitness covariance `Ω` of its own:

```{julia}
step_schema(OneTraitModel())[:select], step_schema(model_of(p))[:select]
```

The lowering to the kernel is chosen by the model: the same life cycle `g` is sent to the
one-trait operators by default, and to the operators of two traits with
`model = model_of(p)`. Each refuses a population of the other model:

```{julia}
w = World(p); init_env!(w, Xoshiro(1))
try
    lower(g, :kernel)(w, Xoshiro(2))
catch err
    println(sprint(showerror, err))
end
lower(g, :kernel; model = model_of(p))(w, Xoshiro(2)); w.gen
```

`simulate` and `run_composed` choose the model from the `Params`. The records keep
QTSim's columns, which describe trait 1, and add the mean vector, `G` and `P`, the lag
`θ − z̄` and the selection differential, one vector or matrix per recorded generation:

```{julia}
o = simulate(Params(p; NoGenerations = 200); seed = 1)
o.trait_mean[end], o.gmatrix[end]
```

## The G matrix at mutation–selection balance

Each locus's share of `G` loses `(G/2L)(A + G)⁻¹(G/2L)` to selection for good, with
`A = Ω + V_E I`, while the rest of selection's reduction is linkage disequilibrium that
recombination breaks up. Without drift the equilibrium of this multilocus Gaussian model
is the solution of `G (A + G)⁻¹ G = 2L·M` (`gaussian_G_loci`), which for one trait is
QTLSim's `gaussian_vg_loci` [@Lande1980; @Lande1975]. Drift among `N` adults lowers it
(`gaussian_G_loci(p; drift = true)`), and the moments lowering (`run_moments`) iterates
the same recursion generation by generation. Twelve replicate populations, from
genotypes of zero, averaged over generations 1000–2999:

```{julia}
R = 12
runs = Vector{Any}(undef, R)
Threads.@threads :greedy for r in 1:R
    runs[r] = simulate(p; seed = 100 + r)
end
window(o, lo, hi) = findall(t -> lo <= t <= hi, o.gen)
Gk = [mean(o.gmatrix[window(o, 1000, 2999)]) for o in runs]
Gbar = mean(Gk)
Gth, Gd = gaussian_G_loci(p), gaussian_G_loci(p; drift = true)
Gmo = run_moments(p; erosion = true).gmatrix[end]
corr(G) = G[1, 2] / sqrt(G[1, 1] * G[2, 2])
angle(v) = mod(atand(v[2], v[1]), 180)
```

```{julia}
#| output: asis
println("| | G₁₁ | G₁₂ | G₂₂ | genetic correlation | g_max (degrees from trait 1) |\n|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|")
se(f) = std(f.(Gk)) / sqrt(R)
@printf("| kernel, 12 runs (± SE) | %.4f ± %.4f | %.4f ± %.4f | %.4f ± %.4f | %.3f ± %.3f | %.1f |\n",
        Gbar[1, 1], se(G -> G[1, 1]), Gbar[1, 2], se(G -> G[1, 2]), Gbar[2, 2], se(G -> G[2, 2]),
        corr(Gbar), se(corr), angle(gmax(Gbar)))
for (nm, G) in (("multilocus Gaussian, with drift (`gaussian_G_loci(p; drift = true)`)", Gd),
                ("moments lowering, with drift (`run_moments(p; erosion = true)`)", Gmo),
                ("multilocus Gaussian, no drift (`gaussian_G_loci(p)`)", Gth))
    @printf("| %s | %.4f | %.4f | %.4f | %.3f | %.1f |\n", nm, G[1, 1], G[1, 2], G[2, 2], corr(G), angle(gmax(G)))
end
@printf("| mutation, `M` | %.4f | %.4f | %.4f | %.3f | %.1f |\n", M[1, 1], M[1, 2], M[2, 2], corr(M), angle(gmax(M)))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
ratio = [Gbar[1, 1] / Gd[1, 1], Gbar[2, 2] / Gd[2, 2]]
@printf("The kernel's variances are %.2f and %.2f times the prediction with drift, and its genetic correlation %.3f against %.3f: ",
        ratio..., corr(Gbar), corr(Gd))
@printf("the Gaussian approximation somewhat overestimates the variances and gets their correlation right (`validate/moments_loci.jl` compares it with the kernel systematically). ")
@printf("The leading axis of `G`, `g_max`, lies at %.0f° from trait 1 (%.0f° predicted), against %.0f° for `M`: ",
        angle(gmax(Gbar)), angle(gmax(Gd)), angle(gmax(M)))
@printf("Lande's equilibrium mixes the mutational and the selective covariances (for weak mutation it is their matrix geometric mean), so `G` is not a scaled copy of `M`.\n")
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-g
#| fig-cap: "The G matrix at equilibrium, as ellipses of points x with xᵀG⁻¹x = 1. Thin grey: each of the 12 kernel runs; black: their mean; red dashed: the multilocus Gaussian prediction with drift; blue dotted: the mutational covariance M, scaled to the same area."
ellipse(G; n = 100) = (F = eigen(Symmetric(G)); [F.vectors * (sqrt.(F.values) .* [cos(t), sin(t)]) for t in range(0, 2π, n)])
pts(G) = (e = ellipse(G); (first.(e), last.(e)))
fig = Figure(size = (420, 400))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], aspect = DataAspect(), xlabel = "trait 1", ylabel = "trait 2")
for G in Gk
    lines!(ax, pts(G)..., color = (:grey, 0.5), linewidth = 0.8)
end
lines!(ax, pts(Gbar)..., color = :black, linewidth = 2, label = "kernel")
lines!(ax, pts(Gd)..., color = :crimson, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 2, label = "theory")
Ms = M .* sqrt(abs(QTLSim.det(Gbar)) / abs(QTLSim.det(M)))
lines!(ax, pts(Ms)..., color = :steelblue, linestyle = :dot, linewidth = 2, label = "M (scaled)")
axislegend(ax, position = :rb)
fig
```

## Correlated response and the line of least resistance

Selection on one trait moves the others through their genetic covariances. Lande's
response is `Δz̄ = G β` with the selection gradient `β = (A + G)⁻¹(θ − z̄)`
[@Lande1979; @LandeArnold1983]: in `G`'s eigenbasis each component of `β` is multiplied
by its eigenvalue, so the response turns from the gradient toward `g_max`, the genetic line
of least resistance [@Schluter1996]. For an optimum moving at a constant rate `k` (a
vector) the population settles at the lag `λ = (A + G) G⁻¹ k` (`steady_lag_vector`): the
mean keeps up exactly along `k`, but the lag is longest, and points, where there is
least genetic variance. Here the optimum moves by 0.002 per generation from generation
3000, at 70° from trait 1:

```{julia}
pm = Params(p; NoGenerations = 5000, MoveFitnessSDGen = 3000, MoveType = :continuous,
            MoveFitnessSD = 0.002, MoveDirection = [cosd(70), sind(70)])
mruns = Vector{Any}(undef, R)
Threads.@threads :greedy for r in 1:R
    mruns[r] = simulate(pm; seed = 200 + r)
end
lagk = mean(mean(o.trait_lag[window(o, 4000, 4999)]) for o in mruns)
Gm = mean(mean(o.gmatrix[window(o, 4000, 4999)]) for o in mruns)
k = 0.002 .* move_direction(pm)
λth = steady_lag_vector(k; G = Gm, A = selection_variance_matrix(pm))
mo = run_moments(pm; erosion = true)
λmo = mean(mo.trait_lag[4001:5000])
d = response_deflection(λth; G = Gm, A = selection_variance_matrix(pm))
```

```{julia}
#| output: asis
println("| | lag, trait 1 | lag, trait 2 | direction (degrees) |\n|:--|--:|--:|--:|")
for (nm, v) in (("kernel, generations 4000–4999", lagk), ("`steady_lag_vector`, kernel's G", λth),
                ("moments lowering", λmo), ("the optimum's motion `k` (×10)", 10 .* k))
    @printf("| %s | %.4f | %.4f | %.1f |\n", nm, v[1], v[2], mod(atand(v[2], v[1]), 360))
end
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
@printf("The optimum moves at 70°, `g_max` lies at %.0f°, and the lag points at %.0f° in the kernel (%.0f° predicted): ",
        angle(gmax(Gm)), mod(atand(lagk[2], lagk[1]), 360), mod(atand(λth[2], λth[1]), 360))
@printf("it is deflected away from `g_max`, toward the direction of least genetic variance, while the gradient it creates, `β`, is turned by `G` back onto the optimum's path. ")
@printf("At the steady lag the response `Gβ` lies at %.1f° from `g_max` and the gradient `β` at %.1f°: selection pulls off the line of least resistance, and `G` turns the response back toward it.\n",
        d.angle_response_gmax, d.angle_gradient_gmax)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-lag
#| fig-cap: "Tracking an optimum that moves at 70° from trait 1. Left: the mean phenotype (black, mean of 12 runs) and the optimum (red) in the plane of the two traits from generation 3000; the dashed line is the g_max axis through the mean at 3000. Right: the lag θ − z̄, each run's mean over generations 4000–4999 (grey), their mean (black) and the steady lag vector (red cross)."
fig = Figure(size = (820, 380))
ax1 = Axis(fig[1, 1], aspect = DataAspect(), xlabel = "trait 1", ylabel = "trait 2", title = "mean and optimum")
zt = [mean(o.trait_mean[i] for o in mruns) for i in 3001:10:5000]
θt = [mean(o.trait_mean[i] + o.trait_lag[i] for o in mruns) for i in 3001:10:5000]
lines!(ax1, first.(θt), last.(θt), color = :crimson, label = "optimum")
lines!(ax1, first.(zt), last.(zt), color = :black, label = "mean")
gm = gmax(Gm); z0 = zt[1]
lines!(ax1, [z0[1] - 2gm[1], z0[1] + 2gm[1]], [z0[2] - 2gm[2], z0[2] + 2gm[2]], color = :grey, linestyle = :dash, label = "g_max")
axislegend(ax1, position = :lt)
ax2 = Axis(fig[1, 2], aspect = DataAspect(), xlabel = "lag, trait 1", ylabel = "lag, trait 2", title = "the lag")
lr = [mean(o.trait_lag[window(o, 4000, 4999)]) for o in mruns]
scatter!(ax2, first.(lr), last.(lr), color = (:grey, 0.7))
scatter!(ax2, [lagk[1]], [lagk[2]], color = :black, markersize = 14)
scatter!(ax2, [λth[1]], [λth[2]], color = :crimson, marker = :xcross, markersize = 18)
lines!(ax2, [0, 0.05cosd(70)], [0, 0.05sind(70)], color = :crimson, linestyle = :dot)
scatter!(ax2, [0.0], [0.0], color = :black, marker = :cross)
fig
```

## Pleiotropy and the mutational correlation

How much of the genetic correlation between two traits comes from the mutations, and how
much from selection? Lande's equilibrium answers it: `G` is shaped by both `M` and `A`,
and with weak mutation it is their geometric mean, so a mutational correlation `r_μ` is
carried into `G` but pulled toward the correlation that selection favours
[@Lande1980; @Jones2003]. With `M = m V_E [1 r_μ; r_μ 1]` and selection uncorrelated
(`SelCorr = 0`) or correlated (`SelCorr = 0.5`), four runs each:

```{julia}
rμs = [-0.6, -0.3, 0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9]
rωs = [0.0, 0.5]
pc = Params(p; MutCov = zeros(0, 0), PopSize = 500, NoGenerations = 2500)
cases = [(rμ, rω) for rω in rωs for rμ in rμs]
pcase(rμ, rω) = Params(pc; MutCorr = rμ, SelCorr = rω)
cjobs = [(i, r) for i in eachindex(cases) for r in 1:4]
cres = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(cjobs))
Threads.@threads :greedy for j in eachindex(cjobs)
    i, r = cjobs[j]
    o = simulate(pcase(cases[i]...); seed = 300 + 10i + r)
    cres[j] = corr(mean(o.gmatrix[window(o, 1000, 2499)]))
end
rG = [mean(cres[j] for j in eachindex(cjobs) if cjobs[j][1] == i) for i in eachindex(cases)]
rGse = [std([cres[j] for j in eachindex(cjobs) if cjobs[j][1] == i]) / 2 for i in eachindex(cases)]
rGth(rμ, rω) = corr(gaussian_G_loci(pcase(rμ, rω); drift = true))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-rmu
#| fig-cap: "The genetic correlation at equilibrium against the mutational correlation, with uncorrelated selection (black) and with a fitness correlation of 0.5 (red). Points: kernel, mean of 4 runs with ±1 SE; lines: the multilocus Gaussian equilibrium with drift; grey: r_G = r_μ."
fig = Figure(size = (460, 380))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "mutational correlation r_μ", ylabel = "genetic correlation r_G")
xs = range(-0.6, 0.9, 40)
lines!(ax, [-0.6, 0.9], [-0.6, 0.9], color = :grey80)
for (rω, col) in zip(rωs, (:black, :crimson))
    lines!(ax, xs, [rGth(x, rω) for x in xs], color = col, label = "SelCorr = $rω")
    ii = findall(c -> c[2] == rω, cases)
    errorbars!(ax, rμs, rG[ii], rGse[ii], color = col, whiskerwidth = 6)
    scatter!(ax, rμs, rG[ii], color = col)
end
axislegend(ax, position = :lt)
fig
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
i0 = findfirst(==((0.0, 0.5)), cases)
dev = maximum(abs(rG[i] - rGth(cases[i]...)) for i in eachindex(cases))
@printf("The kernel follows the prediction across the range: the largest difference in r_G is %.3f. ", dev)
@printf("A positive fitness correlation (individuals far off along both traits together are selected less against, `Ω` elongated along (1, 1)) maintains more variance along (1, 1), so with uncorrelated mutations r_G is %.2f (%.2f predicted), not zero. ",
        rG[i0], rGth(0.0, 0.5))
@printf("The genetic correlation is a compromise between the mutational and the selective correlations, not a copy of either.\n")
```

## Local adaptation across demes

Steps carry parameters of their model, so a deme can be given an optimum vector of its own:
`withparams(g, p; θ = [θ₁, θ₂])` is the generation of a deme selected toward
`(θ₁, θ₂)`. Four demes of 100 diploids with optima at distance 2 from the origin, at 0°,
60°, 120° and 180°, exchange migrants at forward rate 0.01 (island model). The moments
lowering of several demes (`between = true`) carries, for each deme, the haplotype
moments of the multilocus model as matrices and, with drift, the cross-moments between
demes, so it predicts the deme means, the within-deme `G` and the covariance matrix of
the deme means. Twenty kernel runs:

```{julia}
pd = Params(Ploidy = 2, NoQTL = 20, PhenotypeVar = 2.0, Heritability = 0.5, MutationScalar = 1e-3,
            MutationRatePerGamete = 0.02, PopSize = 100, NoGenerations = 3000, Sample = 10, InitFitnessSD = 5.0,
            NoTraits = 2, MutCorr = 0.3, SelCorr = 0.2)
φs = [0.0, 60.0, 120.0, 180.0]
θs = [2.0 .* [cosd(φ), sind(φ)] for φ in φs]
dcycle = foldl(⊗, [withparams(g, pd; θ = θ) for θ in θs]) ⋅ L.migrate(4)
census = collect(1500:10:2990)
function deme_run(seed)
    s = pd ⊗ demes(4)
    idx = IdDict(w => i for (i, w) in enumerate(s.demes))
    mg = [zeros(2) for _ in 1:4, _ in census]
    gw = [zeros(2, 2) for _ in 1:4, _ in census]
    rec = operator(:record, function (w, rng)
        j = searchsortedfirst(census, w.gen)
        if j <= length(census) && census[j] == w.gen
            gt = traitvalues(w; what = :genotype)
            mg[idx[w], j] = vec(mean(gt; dims = 2)); gw[idx[w], j] = cov(gt; dims = 2)
        end
        w
    end)
    run_composed(s, Xoshiro(seed); cycle = dcycle, record = false, images = Dict(:record => rec), migration_rate = 0.01)
    (means = [mean(mg[a, :]) for a in 1:4], W = mean(gw),
     A = mean(cov(reduce(hcat, mg[:, j]); dims = 2) for j in eachindex(census)))
end
dres = Vector{Any}(undef, 20)
Threads.@threads :greedy for r in 1:20
    dres[r] = deme_run(400 + r)
end
dm = run_moments(pd; cycle = dcycle, migration_rate = 0.01, between = true)
sel = findall(in(census), dm.metapop.gen)
Wm, Am = mean(dm.metapop.within[sel]), mean(dm.metapop.var_among[sel])
rows = findall(in(census), dm.gen)
mmeans = [mean(dm.trait_mean[r] for r in rows if dm.deme[r] == a) for a in 1:4]
kmeans = [mean(x.means[a] for x in dres) for a in 1:4]
qst(W, A) = (σ2 = 3 / 4 .* (A .- W ./ 100); [σ2[i, i] / (σ2[i, i] + 2W[i, i]) for i in 1:2])
```

```{julia}
#| output: asis
println("| deme | optimum | kernel mean | moments mean | direction, kernel | direction, moments |\n|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|")
for a in 1:4
    @printf("| %d | (%.2f, %.2f) | (%.3f, %.3f) | (%.3f, %.3f) | %.1f° | %.1f° |\n", a, θs[a]..., kmeans[a]..., mmeans[a]...,
            atand(kmeans[a][2], kmeans[a][1]), atand(mmeans[a][2], mmeans[a][1]))
end
Wk, Ak = mean(x.W for x in dres), mean(x.A for x in dres)
println("\n| | G₁₁ | G₁₂ | G₂₂ | among, 11 | among, 12 | among, 22 | Q_ST trait 1 | Q_ST trait 2 |\n|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|")
@printf("| kernel, 20 runs | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f |\n", Wk[1, 1], Wk[1, 2], Wk[2, 2],
        Ak[1, 1], Ak[1, 2], Ak[2, 2], qst(Wk, Ak)...)
@printf("| moments, `between = true` | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f | %.3f |\n", Wm[1, 1], Wm[1, 2], Wm[2, 2],
        Am[1, 1], Am[1, 2], Am[2, 2], qst(Wm, Am)...)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
fst0 = neutral_deme_variances(backward_migration(island_migration(4, 0.01), 100), 100, muteVar(pd); origins = :exchange).qst
qk, qm = qst(Wk, Ak), qst(Wm, Am)
@printf("The demes do not reach their optima: migration pulls each toward the others, so the deme whose optimum is at 0° has its mean at %.0f° and the one at 180° at %.0f°. ",
        atand(kmeans[1][2], kmeans[1][1]), atand(kmeans[4][2], kmeans[4][1]))
@printf("Trait 1, along which the optima are spread further, is more differentiated than trait 2: Q_ST is %.3f and %.3f in the kernel (%.3f and %.3f predicted), against %.3f for a neutral trait in the same metapopulation. ",
        qk..., qm..., fst0)
@printf("The largest difference between the kernel's and the moments' deme means is %.3f, for optima at distance 2.\n",
        maximum(maximum(abs.(kmeans[a] .- mmeans[a])) for a in 1:4))
```

`validate/trait_moments_demes.jl` makes this comparison with 200 runs and 50 loci, with
tolerances fixed before the runs, and passes:

```{julia}
#| output: asis
logf = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "..", "validate", "trait_moments_demes.log")
if isfile(logf)
    inT1 = false
    for l in readlines(logf)
        occursin("T1 local", l) && (inT1 = true)
        occursin("deme means", l) && (inT1 = false)
        (inT1 || startswith(l, "PASS") || startswith(l, "FAIL")) && println("    ", l)
    end
end
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-demes
#| fig-cap: "Four demes adapting to optima at 0°, 60°, 120° and 180° (crosses), linked by migration. Points: the kernel's deme means (20 runs, each run's mean over generations 1500–2990, light; their mean, dark); open circles: the moments lowering; ellipses: the within-deme G of the moments (×1), centred on each deme's mean."
fig = Figure(size = (520, 420))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], aspect = DataAspect(), xlabel = "trait 1", ylabel = "trait 2")
cols = Makie.wong_colors()
for a in 1:4
    scatter!(ax, [θs[a][1]], [θs[a][2]], marker = :xcross, markersize = 16, color = cols[a])
    scatter!(ax, [x.means[a][1] for x in dres], [x.means[a][2] for x in dres], color = (cols[a], 0.35), markersize = 6)
    scatter!(ax, [kmeans[a][1]], [kmeans[a][2]], color = cols[a], markersize = 12)
    scatter!(ax, [mmeans[a][1]], [mmeans[a][2]], color = :white, strokecolor = :black, strokewidth = 1.5, markersize = 12)
    e = ellipse(Wm)
    lines!(ax, mmeans[a][1] .+ first.(e), mmeans[a][2] .+ last.(e), color = (cols[a], 0.6))
end
fig
```

## A fluctuating optimum

The optimum vector can also fluctuate around its trend: as a cycle along a direction `f`
(`MoveType = :periodic`, `FluctDirection`), or as red noise, a vector AR(1) process with a
stationary covariance `Σ` (`MoveType = :red_noise`, `MoveNoiseCov`, by default
`MoveNoiseSD² f fᵀ`) and autocorrelation `ρ`. The lag then fluctuates too. With the
mean following `z̄' = z̄ + B (θ − z̄)`, `B = G (A + G)⁻¹`, the lag and the noise form a
linear system whose stationary covariance solves a discrete Lyapunov equation;
`red_noise_lag_cov(Σ, ρ; G, A)` is its lag block, the matrix version of the one-trait
`red_noise_lag_var` (vignette 06), and `periodic_lag_cov` that of `periodic_response`.
Twelve runs with `Σ = [0.2 0.05; 0.05 0.1]` and `ρ = 0.7`, the lag's covariance over
generations 1500–2499:

```{julia}
pf = Params(p; PopSize = 500, NoQTL = 10, NoGenerations = 2500, MoveFitnessSDGen = 1000, MoveFitnessSD = 0.0,
            MoveType = :red_noise, MoveNoiseCov = [0.2 0.05; 0.05 0.1], MoveAutocorr = 0.7)
fruns = Vector{Any}(undef, R)
Threads.@threads :greedy for r in 1:R
    fruns[r] = simulate(pf; seed = 500 + r)
end
Λk = mean(mean(l * l' for l in o.trait_lag[window(o, 1500, 2499)]) for o in fruns)
Gf = mean(mean(o.gmatrix[window(o, 1500, 2499)]) for o in fruns)
Λth = red_noise_lag_cov(pf.MoveNoiseCov, 0.7; G = Gf, A = selection_variance_matrix(pf))
@printf("E[λλᵀ]: kernel [%.4f %.4f; %.4f %.4f], red_noise_lag_cov with the kernel's G [%.4f %.4f; %.4f %.4f]\n",
        Λk[1, 1], Λk[1, 2], Λk[2, 1], Λk[2, 2], Λth[1, 1], Λth[1, 2], Λth[2, 1], Λth[2, 2])
@printf("expected lag load tr((Ω + P)⁻¹ E[λλᵀ])/2 = %.4f\n", trait_lag_load(Params(pf); G = Gf))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
@printf("The theory has the lag's covariance to within %.0f%% on the diagonal and %.0f%% off it. ",
        100 * maximum(abs(Λk[i, i] / Λth[i, i] - 1) for i in 1:2), 100 * abs(Λk[1, 2] / Λth[1, 2] - 1))
@printf("The excess on the diagonal, %.4f and %.4f, is about the same for both traits: it is what the deterministic theory leaves out, the drift of the mean and the sampling error of the recorded mean phenotype, which add to the lag in every direction.\n",
        Λk[1, 1] - Λth[1, 1], Λk[2, 2] - Λth[2, 2])
```

## Kernel and SLiM

The lowering to SLiM's Eidos has its own table of images for several traits: an
individual carries `L·n` values per chromosome, fitness is computed with `matrixMult`,
and mutations are drawn with `rmvnorm`. A step's own vector optimum, fitness covariance,
move direction and mutational covariance become literals in its code, so demes of a SLiM
model can differ in their trait parameters through steps. The generated model is compared
with the kernel, 40 runs each, by two-sample KS tests, in
`validate/slim/compare_traits.jl` (stabilising selection and a moving optimum) and
`validate/slim/compare_traits_fluctuating.jl` (red noise and a cycle, which also compares
the kernel's lag covariance with the theory above). From their logs:

```{julia}
#| output: asis
for f in ("valid_traits.log", "valid_traits_fluctuating.log")
    path = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "..", "validate", "slim", f)
    isfile(path) || continue
    println("`$f`:\n")
    for l in readlines(path)
        (startswith(l, "smallest") || startswith(l, "theory:")) && println("- ", strip(l))
    end
    println()
end
```

## Where next

- The equilibrium `G` assumes Gaussian allelic effects at every locus; with rare
  mutations of large effect (the house-of-cards regime) it fails for one trait
  ([Mutation–selection balance](../02_mutation_selection_balance/02_mutation_selection_balance.qmd)),
  and for several the shape of `G`, not only its size, should change.
- `G` itself evolves under a moving optimum [@Jones2004], and the mutation matrix can
  evolve [@Jones2007]; the records here keep `G` every generation, so its orientation
  and stability can be followed directly.
- Demography: `Demography = :beverton_holt` works with several traits, so rescue in two
  dimensions, where the lag's direction matters for the load
  (`trait_lag_load`), is a few lines away
  ([Demography and evolutionary rescue](../10_demography_and_rescue/10_demography_and_rescue.qmd)).
- Per-deme trait parameters in a SLiM model go through steps, `withparams(g, p; θ = …)`;
  `slim_script` with one `Params` per deme still requires the demes' trait fields to agree.
